newsitem.title: UK: Report reveals "black holes" in UK finances-papers.
newsitem.headline: Report reveals "black holes" in UK finances-papers.

text.p: An official report due out shortly will expose a multi-billion-pound (dollar) fiscal shortfall from Britain's Conservative era that will create difficulties for the new Labour government's first budget, two newspapers reported on Sunday.

The Sunday Times and Observer said the report, to be released next week, would reveal "black holes" worth billions of pounds in the financial plans Britain's new Labour government inherited when it came to power on May 1.

The shortfall will pose a serious challenge to Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown in drawing up his first budget, which he is due to present to parliament on July, the Sunday Times and the Observer said.
The report, handled by the National Audit Office (NAO), was ordered by Brown in his mission to open the government's finances to public scrutiny.
It will focus on the previous Conservative government's 800 million pound ($1.3 billion) crackdown on fraud and tax evasion, which was supposed to save 6.7 billion pounds over three years.

It will also question the assumptions made in the last budget of Brown's predecessor, Kenneth Clarke, about interest rates, economic growth and hoped-for declines in unemployment which were projected to cut welfare spending, the newspapers said.
Brown has won the confidence of Britain's financial community by his pledges to keep tight control over government spending.

But the newspapers said the revelations in the NAO report may put him under pressure to abandon election manifesto commitments to increase spending on education and to leave personal taxes unchanged. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
